title: Greet by name
instructorPromptText: Write a function that takes a person's name (a string) and returns a friendly greeting like 'Hello, Alice!'.

specGateDimensions.description: What should the function return when the name is an empty string — 'Hello, !' or some other fallback like 'Hello, friend!'?
specGateDimensions.rationale: Empty string is the canonical missed case; forcing a commitment here surfaces whether the student has thought past the happy path.

specGateDimensions.description: Should leading/trailing whitespace in the name be stripped, or preserved verbatim in the greeting?
specGateDimensions.rationale: Students rarely think about input hygiene; surfacing it in the spec prevents output like 'Hello,   Alice  !'.

specGateDimensions.description: Does the function return the greeting string or print it?
specGateDimensions.rationale: Novices routinely conflate return and print; the prompt says 'returns' but students often write print() and then cannot use the result.

expectedDivergences.pattern: Student uses print() instead of return, so the function technically outputs the greeting but returns None
Plan describes string concatenation with '+'; code uses an f-string — coherent idiomatic substitution
Forgets the comma or exclamation mark, producing 'Hello Alice' or 'Hello, Alice' instead of the specified format
Spec committed to stripping whitespace but code passes the name through unchanged
